card.name: Address terms in quoted speech
card.fires_on: Words in quoted dialogue where someone addresses another person with a title or kinship term, such as 'my mother', 'Mommy', 'sir' or 'my Lord', and the comma or quote mark right after it.

modes.label: Kinship address
modes.description: Child or speaker calling out to a parent in quoted speech, on 'my' or the parent word.
modes.example: "My mother<<,>> get up, my father, get up

modes.label: Title of respect
modes.description: Honorific such as sir or Lord used to address someone, and the punctuation that follows it.
modes.example: late; Mr. Gladstone, sir<<,>> is full. He got his 1

modes.label: Opening quote of speech
modes.description: Opening quote mark where a speaker begins an address or declaration.

card.writes: It pushes toward honorific and servant-style address words such as 'sir', '老爷' and '妾', and away from imperial or first-person words.
card.plain: It fires when a character in a story addresses someone as mother, sir or Lord.
